cards.title: The pill box is not the problem
cards.body: Most organisers fail because of how they're filled, not the box itself. A few small habits make the weekly box actually work.

cards.title: Pick morning, afternoon, night slots
cards.body: Match the box to the prescription pattern. For 1-0-1, you need morning and night slots that are easy to tell apart.

cards.title: Fill it from the prescription
cards.body: Not from memory, and not by copying last week's box. Keep the latest prescription next to you and fill one day at a time.

cards.title: Fill on a fixed day
cards.body: Sunday morning with chai works. Same day every week means nobody wonders whether it's been done.

cards.title: Half tablets need care
cards.body: If a dose is half a tablet, ask the chemist whether that tablet can be split and how. Some shouldn't be. A tablet cutter helps.

cards.title: Keep the strips anyway
cards.body: Store the original strips nearby. They carry the name, strength and expiry that the box can't show.

cards.title: Dose changed? Refill the box
cards.body: When the doctor changes a dose, empty and refill the affected slots straight away. Old pills in new slots cause mix-ups.

cards.title: Simple, weekly, checked
cards.body: One box, one fill day, one person responsible, and a quick glance on your video call. That's the whole system.

takeaway: Fill the organiser weekly from the latest prescription, keep the original strips, and ask the chemist before splitting tablets.
share: Send this to the one who fills Nani's pill box every Sunday.
